successCriteria.description: leave.model.ts exports LeaveRequestStatus enum with values DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED
leave.model.ts exports LeaveType enum with values annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity

leave.model.ts exports LeaveRequest interface with all fields: id, employeeId, leaveTypeId, startDate, endDate, daysRequested, reason, status, approvedBy, approvedAt, rejectedBy, rejectedAt, rejectionReason, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, createdAt, updatedAt
leave.model.ts exports CreateLeaveRequestDto with fields employeeId, leaveTypeId, startDate, endDate, reason
leave.model.ts exports UpdateLeaveRequestDto with all-optional fields startDate, endDate, reason
leave.model.ts exports LeaveRequestQueryParams with all-optional fields status, leaveTypeId, startDateFrom, startDateTo, endDateFrom, endDateTo, limit, offset
leave.validation.ts exports createLeaveRequestSchema (Zod) validating CreateLeaveRequestDto with all required fields present and correctly typed
leave.validation.ts exports updateLeaveRequestSchema (Zod) validating UpdateLeaveRequestDto with all fields optional
leave.validation.ts exports leaveRequestQuerySchema (Zod) validating LeaveRequestQueryParams with all fields optional and correctly typed (limit/offset as numbers, dates as strings)
leave.repository.ts exports ILeaveRepository interface with methods: findById(id), findByEmployeeId(employeeId, params), create(dto), update(id, dto), delete(id), findAll(params)
leave.repository.ts exports KnexLeaveRepository class implementing ILeaveRepository, using pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts via Knex
tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.repository.test.ts contains Jest unit tests covering all ILeaveRepository methods with mocked database

constraints: GP-001: All database access must go through the repository layer — KnexLeaveRepository implements ILeaveRepository using Knex over the shared pg Pool
GP-003: All inputs must be validated at boundaries — Zod schemas (createLeaveRequestSchema, updateLeaveRequestSchema, leaveRequestQuerySchema) validate DTOs and query params
No `any` type — use `unknown` with type guards; existing code uses `Record<string, unknown>` in toLeaveRequest mapping
No direct database access outside repository — KnexLeaveRepository is the sole database access point for leave_request table
Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) — all interface fields are explicitly typed, nullable fields use `string | null`
LeaveType enum values must be UPPERCASE per ARCHITECTURE.md canonical block: ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY, UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY
Database column naming uses snake_case (employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, etc.); TypeScript interfaces use camelCase with toLeaveRequest mapping
outOfScope: Business rule enforcement (BR-001 through BR-012: employee active check, date validity, balance sufficiency, overlap detection, notice periods, etc.) — deferred to Phase 2 (leave.service.ts)
Audit record creation (GP-002) on state-changing operations — deferred to Phase 2 service layer
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) at API boundaries — deferred to Phase 3 controller and Phase 4 routes
Leave balance deduction/restoration logic — deferred to Phase 2+ when balance module is integrated
Notification triggers on leave lifecycle events — deferred to Phase 2+
Fastify routes, controllers, and module registration (POST /leave, PATCH /leave/:id/approve, etc.) — deferred to Phases 3 and 4
Cross-module integration (employee, policy, balance, notification, audit modules) — this phase only establishes the leave module's own model, validation, and repository
